phenotype_specificity.statement: Per-person Table 1 rows show early-onset umbilical stump and/or skin and soft-tissue disease, as described for the cohort. CD18 deficiency is stated for all patients at cohort level only. No testing of other genes is reported.

quotes.quote: | **P18** | ♀ | + | 1♀ (died-2 m-sepsis) | 0.5 | 8 | 7.5 | Yes | Yes | FTT, enteropathy | died (1y) |
Umbilical stump disease and/or skin and soft tissue disease were the first presenting symptoms in all patients included in this study, among many other studies [3, 13–18, 20–23].
By definition, CD18 and CD11b were deficient in all patients (0-4.4%, mean 0.9%; and 0-3.8%, mean 0.53%, respectively).

segregation.statement: No relative was genotyped for this variant. Table 1 lists deceased siblings with an LAD-like history for P18; they were not tested.

quotes.quote: | **P18** | ♀ | + | 1♀ (died-2 m-sepsis) | 0.5 | 8 | 7.5 | Yes | Yes | FTT, enteropathy | died (1y) |
Since the variants are segregated in an autosomal recessive manner, the findings will support genetic counselling for the families as well.

in_trans.statement: Reported homozygous (all patients homozygous except P1). Parental genotypes are not reported, so phase or homozygosity was not confirmed in parents.

functional.statement: No assay of the variant itself. Patient-cell flow cytometry showed CD18/CD11b deficiency, stated for all patients at cohort level; per-person CD18 values are not given (see notes).

quotes.quote: By definition, CD18 and CD11b were deficient in all patients (0-4.4%, mean 0.9%; and 0-3.8%, mean 0.53%, respectively).
Most of the patients (90.2%) had severe CD18 deficiency (< 2% expression), while a few others showed moderate deficiency, and there were no patients with mild deficiency (Fig. 1).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Frameshift duplication, p.(Val103SerfsTer39) (batch HGVS c.306dup); paper: c.306dupA, truncation at amino acid 141.

Most ITGß2 mutations lead to reduced/null expression of β2-integrins on the leukocyte surface [33].

population_data_in_papers.statement: Cohort-level only: the 10 variants the authors call novel were 'not found in ExAC nor1000G'. The paper does not list which 10 variants that sentence covers.

quotes.quote: Out of the 16 identified disease-causing variants; 6 were previously reported, while the remaining 10 were novel and were not found in ExAC nor1000G suggesting heterogeneity in the mutation spectrum for LAD-I.

authors_classification.statement: No per-variant ACMG classification is shown. The Methods say variants were categorised under ACMG guidelines, and the authors call all 16 variants 'disease-causing'.

quotes.quote: In our study, direct Sanger sequencing of the ITGß2 gene revealed 16 disease-causing variants in 28 patients.

The identified variants were categorized as pathogenic/likely pathogenic/variant of uncertain significance (VUS)/likely benign/benign based on American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) guidelines [9].

concerns: Zygosity rests on one cohort-wide sentence ('All patients showed homozygous phenotype except P1'); parental genotypes are not reported.
No per-person CD18 percentage is given; only cohort ranges and the three moderate-deficiency patients (P28, P29, P30) are named.

The paper says this patient's variant was previously reported by the same centre (ref 10, PMID 35482138), yet the Discussion calls the variant novel; the same patient is probably in that earlier paper, which is not in this batch.
The P18 sentence does not itself say 'homozygous'; zygosity comes from the cohort-wide sentence.
A different variant at the same codon, c.307delG, is in P4 (candidate G-lad1-067).
notes_for_panel: One carrier (P18, female, consanguineous; sister died at 2 months of sepsis, untested; FTT, enteropathy; died at 1 year).
